topic: Status mark for He died a death
claim: A cognate object’s head noun “is already implied by the verb” and so “does not normally occur on its own”, with the example marked #: #He died a death.
evidence_summary: Ch. 4, p. 305, marks the same string ? and gives a different kind of reason: “Modification of the noun is just about obligatory”, with ?He died a death and ?He grinned a grin. In CGEL’s notation (p. xii), # marks a semantic or pragmatic anomaly and ? questionable grammaticality.
finding: The two chapters disagree on the kind of deviance, semantic redundancy against a near-obligatory modifier, for one example. Both are hedged (“not normally” on p. 673, “just about” on p. 305) and both marks are weaker than ∗, so the clash is in the kind of deviance, not its strength.
inference: Is He died a death semantically anomalous or of questionable grammaticality?

evidence.passage: §2.1, p. 673. “As the head noun itself is already implied by the verb it does not normally occur on its own”.
evidence.example: Ch. 4, p. 305: ?He died a death; ?He grinned a grin.
evidence.establishes: Two chapters give one example different status marks. The reader checked both marks on page images.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
